learningObjectives: Identify the role of business logic validation in Case processing
Configure data validation on a form and on a Stage using App Studio

elements.description: Validation helps reject inappropriate input before dependent processing. A valid input is necessary, but not a guarantee that every later processing step is error-free. Three requirements:
items: (2) restricted to POSSIBLE VALUES (e.g., valid loan type from a list)
(3) meets BUSINESS CONSTRAINTS (e.g., a historical employment start date is in the past)

elements.term: Field Type/control vs. Business logic validation
items: FIELD TYPE/CONTROL — handles FORMAT validation (e.g., a calendar ensures a valid date format)
BUSINESS LOGIC — handles BUSINESS RULE validation (e.g., 'start date cannot be in the past')

elements.text: Think of Field Type validation as a passport scanner — it checks that the document is a valid passport format. Business logic validation is the customs officer — they check whether you're actually allowed to enter (right age, valid visa, not on a watchlist). Format ≠ business validity.

elements.caption: A suitable control can satisfy a requirement; add the business comparison where the control is insufficient.

bulletPoints: 3 data requirements: right type, possible values, business constraints.
Field Type/control = validates format (date, number, dropdown options).
Business logic = validates business rules (date in past, credit score range).
Choose controls that meet the requirement; add business logic when type or control constraints are insufficient.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Validation on a Form vs. Validation on a Stage

elements.description: Triggered when the user submits the form. If invalid, an error displays inline and submission is blocked until corrected. Use when the user CAN immediately fix the issue (e.g., entered a future date → correct it and resubmit).

Evaluated before entry into the specified Stage. An invalid value prevents entry and displays an error. Configure a way to correct the data or take another action, such as returning to earlier work or closing the Case; a corrective path is not supplied automatically.

elements.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 190" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Submission check and Stage-entry check</title><rect x="10" y="10" width="740" height="170" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="30" y="42" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="var(--pa-brand)">Submission check and Stage-entry check</text><g font-size="14" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)"><text x="30" y="78">Form: submit → invalid-condition error → correct and resubmit.</text><text x="30" y="110">Stage: before entry → reject invalid prerequisite data.</text><text x="30" y="142">Provide a way to correct the issue or take an alternate action.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: Form validation checks submission; Stage validation checks entry prerequisites before entry occurs.

elements.term: Configuring business logic validation in App Studio
elements.description: App Studio supports form-submit validation and Stage-entry validation. The condition describes an invalid value; meeting it displays an error. Stage validation is configured in the Case Type Data Model. A field used on several forms can have different validation conditions at each use; reusing it later does not automatically repeat an earlier check.

An employment-history form can require a past start date while a new-hire form requires a future date. Configure the relevant condition for each use of the field; one historical validation is not a global invariant for every later use.

bulletPoints: Form validation → triggered on SUBMIT. User fixes value and resubmits.
Stage validation → evaluated BEFORE entry into the specified Stage; provide a correction or alternate action.
Key decision: can the user fix it immediately? Yes → form. No → Stage.
Condition defines what is INVALID — error shown when condition is MET.

examPitfalls.title: Form validation triggers on SUBMIT — not on field change
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask when form-level validation fires. Candidates say 'immediately when the user leaves the field.' Form validation runs when the user submits the form — not on individual field change or blur events.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Business logic validation on a form is triggered when the user SUBMITS the form — not on individual field changes.

examPitfalls.title: Stage validation is before entry, not exit
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not mistake a target Stage entry prerequisite for validation on exit from the previous Stage or form submission inside the target.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Evaluate the target Stage prerequisite before entering it; an invalid value prevents entry.

examPitfalls.title: Use form validation when the user CAN fix the issue immediately
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions present a scenario and ask whether form or Stage validation is appropriate. Candidates always pick Stage validation for 'important' rules. Form validation is correct when the error can be fixed by the user on the current form — Stage validation is for conditions that must be met before the Stage begins.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use form validation when the user can perform an immediate action to correct the data (e.g., enter a valid date). Use Stage validation when the issue may not be immediately resolvable by the user.

examPitfalls.title: Stage validation requires developer-configured resolution options
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Stage-entry validation displays an error and prevents entry. That does not imply automatic navigation to a previous Stage or a generated corrective form.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When Stage validation fails, the developer must configure the functionality that allows users to resolve the error — such as returning to a previous Stage or closing the Case. Pega does not do this automatically.

examPitfalls.title: Field Type validates FORMAT — business logic validates BUSINESS RULES
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether Field Type constraints (like Integer) count as validation. Candidates say yes — they replace separate validation rules. Field Type validation enforces data format (e.g., must be a number); business logic validation enforces business rules (e.g., value must be greater than zero).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The source calendar example checks date representation, not the employment-history constraint. Some controls suffice for their requirements; add business logic when they do not.

examPitfalls.title: Validation condition defines INVALID data — error fires when condition IS met
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a validation condition and ask when the error shows. Candidates say 'when the condition is false.' The validation condition defines what makes data INVALID — the error is shown when the condition IS true (data matches the invalid pattern), not when it is false.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The condition defines what constitutes INVALID data. When the condition IS met (i.e., the data is invalid), the error message is displayed. Think of it as: 'show error when [invalid condition] is true'.

examPitfalls.title: Both validation types configured in App Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether a developer needs Dev Studio to configure Stage validation. Candidates say yes. Both form validation and Stage validation are configured in App Studio — no Dev Studio access is required for these standard validation types.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Both form validation and Stage validation are configured in App Studio. Dev Studio is not required for this feature.

quickRecap.value: Check type, possible values and business constraints appropriate to the data use.
Choose the field type and control that meet the requirement; add business logic where insufficient.
Validates BUSINESS RULES (date in past, credit score range). Configured in App Studio. Condition defines INVALID state — error fires when condition is true.
Triggered on form SUBMIT. Use when user CAN immediately fix the issue. Error blocks the form until corrected.
Check prerequisites BEFORE target Stage entry. Reject invalid entry and provide a correction or alternate action.
Can the user fix it immediately? Yes → form validation. No → Stage validation.
App Studio — no Dev Studio needed.
